comment: Transcribed, not measured here — the same arrangement as zarr.json, and for
the same reason: the harness belongs to someone else and re-running it means
building ten toolchains.
brentp/vcf-bench times eleven language bindings on one task: iterate the rows
of a VCF, pull an integer out of the INFO field, accumulate, report the mean.
That is the only cross-*language* comparison this repository has any line on.
Everything else in ecosystem/ compares @gmod/vcf against older @gmod/vcf,
which says how much it improved and not where it stands beside htslib.
THE FIGURE FOR @gmod/vcf IS FOR v5.0.2. That is the single most important
thing about this file. js-vcf-js/package.json in that repo pins
'@gmod/vcf': '^5.0.2', which is the 2023-era parser — versions.json here pins
v5.0.9 as its *old* side. So the published 24 s predates the 7.2.0 genotype
and line-scanning rewrites entirely, and the number a reader would take from
it understates the current library by whatever those bought.
sweep.ts's vcf arm therefore runs the identical operation (parseLine, then
INFO.AN[0]) on every major, so the v5-to-v7 ratio measured here can be
carried onto this published scale without rebuilding anyone else's stack.
That is a projection and must be labelled as one: different corpus, different
machine, different year.
Caveats to carry with any use of this table:
- Different corpus. Theirs is 30,000 rows of 1000 Genomes chr1
(20201028_CCDG_14151_B01_GRM_WGS_2020-08-05_chr1.recalibrated_variants),
a many-sample joint callset. Ours is 317 variants at 100/1000/3000 samples
from a seeded generator.
- Different question from the one JBrowse cares about. The task never touches
a genotype, and genotypes are what a variant display renders and what
7.2.0 rewrote. This measures line and INFO parsing; results/vcf-scan.md
measures the genotype scan. They are complementary, not competing.
- Not our machine and not our year. Nothing here is comparable to a
millisecond in ecosystem.md.
- The JS entry in that repo was contributed by this project's author, so
treat it as a self-reported entry in someone else's harness rather than as
an independent third-party measurement of @gmod/vcf.
task: iterate rows of a VCF, extract INFO.AN[0], accumulate, report the mean
